title: Check-in and wins: Routing v3 beta and the outage response
gist: Maya leads with wins: the Routing v3 beta is at 11% fewer miles and 94.6% on-time across six fleets (uneven, about 6% in the dense urban fleet), and the team's outage response was strong even though the status page was late.

turns.t: Hey. Hey, can you hear me? My headphones were doing the thing again where they connect to my laptop and my phone at the same time.
Yeah, I got you. Hi.
Hi. How are you? How was your week, or, I guess it's Thursday, how's the week been so far.
It's been a week. Honestly, I'm okay. I'm tired but I'm okay. It's been better than last week, which is a really low bar.
Very low bar. Subterranean bar. Did you at least get the weekend? I feel like I didn't see you online, which I took as a good sign.

I did, mostly. I went up to Point Reyes on Sunday with my sister and just, didn't look at my phone for like six hours. Which was amazing and also slightly terrifying, given the week. I kept thinking I'd come back to forty pages. But nothing caught fire. Well, nothing new caught fire.
That's the dream. Okay, do you want to drive or do you want me to? I had a couple of things but they can wait, they're not urgent.
Let me start with good stuff, because there's actually a lot of it and I feel like it all got buried by the outage.
Please. I would love good stuff.

So, Routing v3 beta. Kenji and I went through the numbers yesterday, it's the six fleets, everything since September eighth. We're at eleven percent fewer miles driven across the beta, and on-time delivery went from ninety-one point two to ninety-four point six. And it's holding, it's not a one-week spike, it's been basically flat at that level for two weeks. Kenji's ETA model is a big chunk of that, the mean error's down to four point three minutes from six point one.
That's, okay, eleven percent is a big number. Like, that's a slide. Is that consistent across the fleets or is one fleet carrying it?

It's not even, which I want to be honest about. The suburban and regional fleets are doing better than average, like thirteen, fourteen percent. The dense urban one is more like six. Which lines up with what we already knew, the ETA model still struggles with dense urban stops and loading dock wait times. Kenji's got a couple of ideas for the dock stuff, he wants to pull in historical dwell times per location. But even six is good. Six percent fewer miles for a grocery fleet is real money.
Yeah, no, even six is good. Okay. Can you send me the per-fleet breakdown? I'd want that before Tom starts putting eleven percent in every deck he sends out.
Ha. Yes. I'll send it today. And honestly that's sort of related to a thing I want to talk about later.
Noted. Ominous. Before that, how do you feel about the GA date? November seventeenth. Gut check, not the official answer.

Gut check, I'd say seventy, seventy-five percent. The solver's in good shape. The risk is the stuff around it, the migration path for the fleets that aren't in the beta, the settings UI for dispatchers, and the urban ETA thing if a big urban fleet is in the first wave. If nothing else lands on the team, I think we make it. If something else lands on the team, it gets a lot shakier. Which, again, is foreshadowing.
Okay. Lots of foreshadowing today. What else?

The outage. I know it was bad, forty-seven minutes, three hundred and twelve fleets, Brightside got hit really hard, their customers got wrong delivery windows. And the status page thing was bad, twenty-six minutes before we posted anything is not okay, and Ravi's already got that in the follow-ups. But the actual response from the team? It was really good. Ravi had the retry storm identified in, like, fifteen minutes. Daniel had the fix for the dispatch workers, the backoff and the circuit breaker, drafted that same night. The postmortem was blameless and it was actually useful, which, you know, not every postmortem is.

Yeah. I read it. It was a good doc. And I thought the comms after were good, even if the status page during was late. Sofia said Jordan at Brightside was, I wouldn't say happy, but he appreciated the writeup. He said it was the first time a vendor had actually explained what happened instead of just saying 'a third-party issue.'

Good. Yeah. So I want to make sure the team hears that from you too, not just from me. Maybe in the eng all-hands, or just a message in the channel. They know I think they did well. It means something different coming from you.

I'll do it. Honestly I should have already. I'll post something today, and I'll call out Ravi and Daniel by name. And Sofia, actually, she was on the phone with Brightside basically the whole afternoon, she took a lot of heat that wasn't hers to take. I want to make sure that gets seen too, because customer success always gets left out of the incident thank-yous.

title: Team capacity and Daniel's burnout risk
gist: Maya says the team is running at about 110% and Daniel is a burnout risk after working the post-outage weekend and doing Harbor & Pine demo prep; Asher takes on making sure Daniel takes Monday off.

turns.t: Okay, so, that's a great segue, but I'm guessing the other side of it is, how's the team actually doing.

Stretched. Like, really stretched. We were already tight going into September with the v3 beta and the onboarding work, and then the outage basically ate a week for three people. And I don't think anyone's fully recovered yet. Ravi's buried in the follow-ups, the Redis config, the status page automation, the retry budgets. Kenji's trying to do urban ETA work and also answer every beta fleet question because he's the one who understands the model. Everyone's doing one and a half jobs.
Who are you worried about?
Daniel. Mostly Daniel.
Yeah. I figured you'd say that.

He worked the whole weekend after the outage. Saturday and Sunday. Nobody asked him to, I want to be clear, I actually told him on Friday to log off. But he was finishing the retry fix, and then he was helping with the Harbor & Pine demo prep on top of that, because Tom wanted the integration story to look really solid for Elena, the Samsara stuff and the Oracle TMS piece. And he's just, he's short in standups this week. He's normally the most patient person on the team and he snapped at Kenji on Tuesday about something really small, like a naming thing in a PR. Kenji was fine about it, but, you know, that's not Daniel.
Hm. Yeah. That's not him at all.

And the thing that scares me is he's our staff engineer, he's everywhere. If Daniel burns out it's not one person, it's like the whole architecture review process slows down, half the on-call escalations go to him, he's the person everyone asks. And he's not going to tell me he's burning out. He's going to tell me he's fine.
Has he taken any time off since the outage?
No. And he's got PTO, he's got like fifteen days banked. I've mentioned it twice. He says 'after v3.' Which is November seventeenth. That's seven weeks away.

Yeah, no. That's not okay. Okay, what if, let me, can I take that one? Like, I'll talk to him and make sure he takes Monday off. Not 'you should take some time,' like, Monday is off, it's on the calendar, it's done. Sometimes it lands differently coming from me, and it takes it off your plate.
Honestly, yes. That would help. He'll argue.
He can argue. I'll tell him the demo stuff is covered and that I'll personally deal with Tom if anything comes up.

Thank you. And I think part of it is he doesn't trust that things won't fall apart if he's gone. Which is partly on me. I need to get a second person up to speed on the dispatch workers so he's not the only one who can touch them. I was going to pair Ravi with him on the retry follow-ups, and that kind of does double duty.
That's smart. What do you need from me on the bigger picture, though? Like, is this a 'we need to cut scope' thing or a 'we need people' thing?

Both, but people don't help this quarter. Even if we close both frontend hires in October, they're not productive on the driver app until, realistically, January. So for Q4 it's a scope thing. I think we're running at, like, a hundred and ten percent, and that's fine for a sprint. It's not fine for a quarter. Which is basically the Q4 planning conversation tomorrow. And honestly, the thing I'd rather we didn't do is pretend we can do everything and then quietly slip three things in December.

title: Tom promising live ETA to Harbor & Pine
gist: Maya learned via Daniel's demo prep that Tom is telling Harbor & Pine live ETA sharing ships this quarter; it's unbuilt, about 5 engineer-weeks, and competes with driver onboarding. Asher agrees it must be a planning decision and will talk to Tom before Friday.

turns.t: Right. Which, okay, you said there was a thing you wanted to talk about. Is it the Tom thing?
It's the Tom thing. Do you already know?
I know there's a Tom thing. I don't know which Tom thing.

Okay. So, Daniel was in the demo prep for Harbor & Pine. And he came back and told me that Tom has been telling them, like Marcus, and I think Elena too, that live ETA sharing is coming this quarter. Like, 'it's on the roadmap for Q4,' in those words. Not maybe, not 'we're exploring it.' This quarter.
Ugh. Okay.

And Asher, it's not built. It's not started. We scoped it at about five engineer-weeks, and that's the optimistic version, that's without the edge cases on the tracking link, without load testing a public page that every end customer is going to hit. And it's directly competing with the driver onboarding work, which is a Q4 OKR. We have thirty-eight percent of new drivers dropping off before their first route. Priya's whole redesign, the phone login, the permissions primer, the practice route, depends on us having engineers for it. So if Tom's promising live ETA this quarter, either onboarding slips or v3 GA slips or Daniel works more weekends, and I'm not doing the third one.
No. Yeah. Agreed.

And I'm honestly, I'm frustrated. Like, this isn't the first time. It's a pattern. Sales commits engineering without asking engineering. And then I find out secondhand from someone on my team who happened to be in the room. If Daniel hadn't been in that demo prep, I would've found out when Marcus asked me about it on a call. Which would've been a great moment.

Yeah. You're right to be frustrated. I think, to be fair to Tom, the deal is real. Three hundred and ten k, it's the biggest deal in the pipeline, RouteWise is undercutting us on price, and the decision's October thirtieth. And Marcus has said live ETA is a must-have, more than once. So I get why Tom's reaching for it. And Marcus isn't the one signing. Dana Whitfield, their CFO, is the economic buyer, she's never been on a call, and Tom's worried that if Marcus can't go to her with a checklist that's all green, she just picks the cheaper option. Which, you know, is RouteWise.

I get it too. I'm not saying don't build it. Brightside's asked for it twice too, and with their renewal in January, honestly it might be the right call. I'm saying it should be a call. Made in planning, with the tradeoff on the table, not made in a sales demo.
If it came to it, though, if planning said we're doing it, what would you cut? Just so I have a sense going into tomorrow.

Honestly I'd want to look at the table before I answer, but my instinct is we don't cut onboarding, because that's a hard OKR and Priya's team has done the research already. I'd probably push some of the v3 GA polish to after GA, like the dispatcher settings UI could ship as a fast follow. And I'd want to ask whether Harbor & Pine actually needs the full thing on day one, or whether a tracking link with just the ETA, no live map, gets Marcus what he needs for Dana. I haven't scoped that, so don't quote me, but that's the conversation I'd want to have. With numbers.

That's really useful. Okay. So, I'll talk to Tom. Before Friday's planning, so tomorrow morning, first thing. I'll tell him we can't keep saying 'this quarter' until it's actually prioritized, and that he needs to bring it to planning as an ask, with the deal context, the dollar number, the timeline, and we'll make the tradeoff there, together. And if we do decide to do it, great, then he can say it. I'd also like you in that conversation with Tom, honestly, or at least I want him hearing the five weeks number from you in planning and not from me secondhand. Otherwise it's the same problem in reverse.
That's all I want. Thank you.
And if he's already put it in writing to them, in an email or a proposal or whatever, we need to know that too. I'll ask him directly.
Yeah, good point. Elena's going to hold him to anything that's in an email. She's very, she reads everything.
